claims.evidence: MaxQuant Experiment names. pride sample protocol: 'primary ESC cultures isolated from healthy EM (n=6), endometriotic EM (n=5) and endometriotic peritoneal lesions (n=5)'; the deposit has exactly 6 ctrl_euESC, 5 euESC and 5 ecESC experiments. ctrl = healthy-woman eutopic ESC, eu = eutopic ESC of endometriosis patients, ec = ectopic (peritoneal lesion) ESC, matching the title's eutopic/ectopic wording.

claims.value: SILAC standard (Lys8/Arg10; secretory-phase ESC + Ishikawa 2:1) spiked into <experiment>
claims.evidence: pride: 'samples were spiked 1:1 with the SILAC standard. The standard consisted of 2:1 secretory phase ESCs and Ishikawa EM cancer cells labelled with heavy isotope lysine and arginine.' One heavy source name per spiked mixture (16), shared by that mixture's fractions and re-injections: these 16 names are aliquots of ONE physical standard pool. Encoding follows curated super-SILAC precedents (PXD009766, PXD000690).

claims.value: SILAC light = patient ESC sample; SILAC heavy = spike-in standard
claims.evidence: Explicit: standard labelled with heavy Lys/Arg; MaxQuant Labels0 empty (light), Labels1 Arg10;Lys8. Data check: epithelial markers of the Ishikawa component (KRT8, EPCAM, CDH1, KRT18) have median log2 H/L +2 to +3.5 and stromal VIM -0.8, i.e. epithelial material is in the heavy channel.

'healthy EM' vs 'endometriotic EM' and 'endometriotic peritoneal lesions'. MONDO:0005133 endometriosis, PATO:0000461 normal. The peritoneal-lesion subtype is carried by organism part, not by a narrower MONDO term, since 'pelvic' is not stated.
Eutopic = endometrium (UBERON:0001295); ectopic = 'endometriotic peritoneal lesions' (UBERON:0002358). Standard: secretory-phase ESCs and Ishikawa (endometrial adenocarcinoma) are both endometrial.

claims.value: stromal cell of endometrium (study samples); not applicable (standard mixes stromal and epithelial cancer cells)
claims.evidence: 'primary ESC cultures' (endometrial stromal cells); PRIDE organism_parts 'Stromal cell of endometrium'. CL:0002255.
PRIDE organism Homo sapiens (human); human primary ESCs and the human Ishikawa line; human UniProt reference proteome searched.
Light = patient ESC lysate; heavy = SILAC spike-in standard (PRIDE:0001013 study sample, PRIDE:0000899 reference).
primary cell cultures; standard = mixture of primary ESCs and a cell line, 'cell' as in precedent PXD009766.
One number per independent primary culture within each factor-value group (spec README.adoc:330; campaign rule 3); numbers equal the deposit's experiment index.

claims.value: not pooled (study samples); SN=secretory-phase endometrial stromal cells;SN=Ishikawa (standard)
claims.evidence: Standard composition from the sample protocol; Ishikawa = CVCL_2529.
Endometrial stromal cells / endometriotic lesions from women ('women of reproductive age'); Ishikawa is female (Cellosaurus). Anatomically determined, not a cohort-summary copy.

claims.value: not available (study samples); pooled / not applicable (standard)
claims.evidence: No individual-level patient table is deposited and the paper is closed access. Whether euESC_n and ecESC_n come from the same woman is not stated in the deposit, so individual is not asserted.

'fractionated into 6 fractions using strong cation exchange and C18 StageTips'.

Paper (J Proteome Res 2016) not read: closed access; only the abstract and the PRIDE protocols were used. Patient age, cycle phase, endometriosis stage, passage number and the eutopic/ectopic pairing are therefore not annotated.
characteristics[individual] = not available: the deposit does not say whether euESC_n and ecESC_n are from the same patient.
Precursor mass tolerance not available (MaxQuant 1.4.0.8 parameters.txt lacks it, no mqpar.xml); parse_sdrf convert-openms fails on it.
Technical replicate 2 = later re-injection of the same SCX fraction (19 files); which injection MaxQuant weighted is not recorded - both were searched (all in experimentalDesignTemplate).

The 16 heavy source names denote aliquots of one physical SILAC standard pool (one name per spiked mixture, per the campaign shared-reference rule); the secretory-phase ESC donors of the standard are not described.
Template versions: the spec submodule's nested sdrf-templates copy is older than upstream 7da1747 (ms-proteomics 1.2.0).
One post-build edit: scripts/concat_fix.py sets comment[fraction identifier] on the 36 re-injection rows (build numbers a one-file row as fraction 1); asserted no main-build row changes.
